\section*{Datasets}

Every dataset above is one packed \texttt{npz} per task at
\texttt{<root>/data/<family>/<task>.npz}, the eight unified fields stacked $[N,T,\cdot]$
(\texttt{observation}, \texttt{action}, \texttt{next\_observation},
\texttt{achieved\_goal}, \texttt{reward}, \texttt{terminal}, \texttt{timeout},
\texttt{success}). \texttt{env/unified.py::load\_packed} flattens to $N\!\cdot\!T$
transitions and \emph{synthesizes} the \texttt{terminals} that mark trajectory boundaries
at each episode's last step: the env's own \texttt{terminal} flag never fires, since every
collection here is fixed-horizon. Two schema facts matter for reading the grid.
(i)~\texttt{achieved\_goal} is a zeros placeholder in all six datasets and is never read.
(ii)~The eval goal for the goal-conditioned critics does not come from the data's goal
field either --- it is the single highest-reward \texttt{next\_observation} in the dataset
(\texttt{env/unified.py:167}), one fixed frame reused for every eval episode. The
\emph{play-resample} arm deliberately leaves this eval-side channel unrepaired.

All statistics in Table~\ref{tab:datasets} were recomputed from the packed files, not
copied from the collection logs. \emph{ep-succ} is the fraction of episodes in which
\texttt{success} ever fires; \emph{dwell} is the fraction of \emph{all} steps spent at the
goal --- the quantity that separates ``reached it'' from ``sat on it''.

\paragraph{\texttt{expert}.}
ManiSkill comes from the published Factor-FB-Offline pack: rollouts of the pretrained newt
TD-MPC2 checkpoints (HF \texttt{nicklashansen/newt}, snapshot \texttt{7eef11e}) with the
planner on and zero exploration, 50 parallel envs, failures kept
(\texttt{success\_only=false}); newt's multitask obs/action padding is stripped back to the
raw env dims. That pack has no \texttt{mw-pick-place}/\texttt{mw-push}, and its play
counterpart is unreachable, so both Metaworld tasks were regenerated from Metaworld's
built-in scripted oracle (\texttt{data\_collection/collect\_mw\_standalone.py}, torch-free,
no checkpoint) through \texttt{env/metaworld\_env.py} --- action-repeat 2, horizon 100,
byte-identical to the eval env. This regime is a saturated single-mode oracle corridor: BC
already solves it, which is why the FB/BC row reads $1.00\pm0.00$ on both Metaworld expert
columns and why no critic can earn its keep there (Ph.~I).

\paragraph{\texttt{play-noise} and \texttt{play-noise-hard}.}
Same collectors, exploration mixture on. Structurally this is still \emph{one target per
episode}, held for the whole horizon, with heavy terminal dwell --- the oracle reaches the
goal and then sits there for roughly half the episode, so the goal marginal collapses onto
a single per-episode point. Only the action distribution differs from \texttt{expert}, not
the goal distribution. \texttt{play-noise-hard} changes nothing but the mixture
($f_{\mathrm{exp}}=0$, $\varepsilon_{\max}=0.5$, $\sigma_{\max}=0.3$); horizon, per-episode
target and dwell are left untouched \emph{on purpose}, so the arm isolates Ph.~I from
Ph.~II/III. It drops the BC floor to $\approx0.5$, which is the entire point: the benchmark
measures guidance quality again rather than measuring the ceiling.

\paragraph{\texttt{play-resample} and \texttt{play-resample-hard}.}
A different \emph{shape} of data, from
\texttt{collect\_mw\_play\_resample.py}:
200 trajectories of 500 wrapper steps ($=1000$ simulator steps, cube-play scale). The target
is re-drawn from the env's own \texttt{goal\_space} and written into
\texttt{raw.\_target\_pos} --- exactly the quantity the observation's goal dims
$\texttt{obs}[36{:}39]$ and the scripted oracle read --- immediately when \texttt{success}
fires (no dwell, as in cube play) and every $\texttt{seg\_max}=60$ steps regardless, so no
segment gets stuck. \texttt{raw.curr\_path\_length} is zeroed before each wrapper step to
defeat Metaworld's $\texttt{max\_path\_length}=500$ truncation. Coverage here comes from
relocation chaining, not action noise, so the mixture is deliberately gentle. Each
trajectory becomes a chain of ${\sim}30\text{--}48$ reach-and-move segments, and
within-trajectory relabeling now crosses target contexts through transitions the data
actually contains (the train-side repair of Ph.~II). The regime nonetheless re-saturates:
everything scores $0.95\text{--}0.98$, BC included. Under the hot mixture the chaining
breaks --- relocations per trajectory collapse by an order of magnitude, because the oracle
rarely completes a segment --- but \texttt{play-resample-hard} is thereby the only arm that
is simultaneously un-saturated \emph{and} goal-diverse, which is what makes it informative.
